reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited paragraphs support it: none of p0029-p0035 (use restrictions), p0095 (mutual confidentiality definition, where 'accounting records for which access is obtained' is definitional scoping only) or p0114 (an examination right running in Sparkling's favour over escrowed source code) grants Garman any audit, inspection, verification or system-access right against us.

Absence of a Vendor audit right is better than the playbook preferred position and benefits our party, so treating it as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct under the rule's protective purpose (AUDIT exists to cap a Vendor-favourable right, not to create one).

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or comment was proposed; the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit, and raising the point would risk inviting a verification right we do not currently owe.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is adequately explained as a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause at all; the rationale documents the search terms and sections reviewed, and preserves the negotiation position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment, no system access) if Garman later tables one.
